evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_opcert_health.py:26: `def opcert_signing_status(binding: Any, repo_root: str | None = None)` — repo_root defaults to None
src/rebar/_mcp_opcert_health.py:53: `status["expected"] = load_trusted_environments(repo_root) is not None` resolves relative to None (cwd) when run_mcp passes no root
dropped.finding: run_mcp calls opcert_signing_status(opcert_binding) with the default repo_root=None (not the composed config root), so the /health opcert field and boot warning resolve .rebar/trusted_environments.yaml relative to the process cwd rather than the composed repo root. store_status deliberately avoids compose_config for the health probe; here trusted-env resolution silently defaults to cwd. If cwd differs from the configured repo root the pinned-key comparison can read the wrong (or no) keyring and mis-report matched/degraded.
